transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: 58 min
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Chu (Redwood PM); Samir Gupta (Head of Platform - Chorus), Lena Ortiz (SRE Lead), Rajiv Menon (CTO), Aisha Khan (FinOps)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Intro + quick Qual: Chorus runs multi-tenant inference (chat + embeddings) for search + tagging; wants per-route cost attribution and guardrails for latency SLOs.
- Console demo: per-route dashboards, cost waterfall, token-level drill, anomaly detection; discussed Dedicated vs Hosted pilot; security questions (SOC2, SAML, KMS) surfaced.
- Agreed next steps: sandbox invite, pilot pricing, workload examples, pilot kickoff.

Topics:
1) Current stack and pain: tagging, chargeback, unpredictable egress spend
2) Console: per-route dashboards, top-N route breakdown, cost waterfall, cost per token vs latency SLOs
3) Optimize suggestions: batching, caching, quantization recommendations
4) Pilot scope and security/compliance checklist

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription has noise):
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining from Redwood side we got Maya and Evan with me uh we'll run through the console and then talk pilot scope.
[00:07] Samir: cool thanks Jordan, quick note, we only have 60 minutes, Rajiv might need to jump for an exec call around 15:15 PT.
[00:13] Jordan: perfect, we'll keep cadence tight. can you give a 2 minute snapshot of what you're seeing today?
[00:20] Samir: yeah uh so Chorus runs a multi-tenant api - mix of chat for product help, embeddings for search and reranking. our problem is cost slicing per product line, um token costs blow up during some batch jobs and then SREs get paged for latency anomalies.
[00:36] Lena: and also the billing mapping is messy - our current tags get lost between app and inference layer, so finance can't map to feature owners.
[00:44] Jordan: okay that tracks, this is a pretty common pattern. we'll show the per-route view in the console which maps requests to route tags and gives you token level unit economics.
[00:53] Maya: quick heads up our console demo includes a cost waterfall across model variants, and Optimize suggestions for batching and kv cache usage - sometimes spelled K-V cache in transcriptions - sorry my notes.
[01:03] Rajiv: when you say model variants, do you mean different quantizations or smaller models? what's the expected delta on cost/latency?
[01:12] Maya: yes both. for example a 4-bit quantized variant of an open model might be 2-3x cheaper but adds tail latency under some seq length distributions; the console surfaces expected tokens/sec and median tail p95 so you can pick the tradeoff.
[01:27] Samir: can we route lower priority requests to a cheaper model automatically?
[01:30] Evan: absolutely — smart routing policies let you set tiers (low cost, standard, high SLO) and fallback rules. the console shows route policies and hit rates.
[01:40] Lena: we need VPC/private deployment options; our data governance team won't allow logs to leave the vpc.
[01:45] Jordan: noted. Redwood Private supports VPC + on-prem packages; we also have audit log export patterns and optional redaction. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[01:54] Aisha: do you have KMS/HSM integration and can we bring our own keys?
[01:58] Maya: yes BYOK via customer KMS is supported; we also have envelope encryption patterns. SOC 2 and ISO are in our compliance deck — i'll share the link.
[02:08] Rajiv: what's the SLA on Dedicated? we can't have more than X% request error rate for real-time chat.
[02:14] Jordan: dedicated capacity has SLA tiers, and we can size capacity based on tokens/sec targets; we'll capture exact numbers in the pilot pricing writeup.
[02:21] -- Console walkthrough starts --
[02:25] Maya: ok i'm going to share the console. you should see the top nav: Routes, Models, Optimize, Billing, Alerts. first panel is the route map — it shows real tenant and path mapping, color coded by spend.
[02:38] [screen reading noise] Maya: here you see Route: /chat/assist-product and Route: /embed/search. the dashboard summarizes tokens, requests, avg latency, p95, and cost per 1000 tokens.
[02:50] Lena: can we break out by customer org id as well?
[02:53] Maya: yes you can group by route, org_id, or feature tag. we have a dimension mapping UI for normalizing tags if your tagging is inconsistent.
[03:02] Samir: show me the cost waterfall.
[03:04] Maya: clicking billing details — waterfall shows model compute, infra (gpu hours normalized), storage (model artifacts + kv cache snapshotting), and misc (network egress). you can toggle to view unit cost per token or cost per session.
[03:16] Maya: notice the spike in compute cost on March 22 — the console links to traces and shows a batch job that incorrectly used the high-tier model for precompute, so you can quickly identify misrouted traffic.
[03:28] Rajiv: nice — do you annotate calls with prompts or user-intent? thats important for us because some routes are long-running system messages.
[03:35] Maya: we capture request meta and show sample prompts in an obfuscated view for privacy. we also support prefix caching and kv cache hit rates; that column helps you see when cache isn't being used.
[03:44] Samir: what about anomalies — do you get automated alerts for spend or latency regressions?
[03:48] Maya: yes anomaly detector flags unusual cost deltas and latency regressions. it ties to evaluations: you can pin a prompt set and get alerted if model quality drops beyond X%.
[03:57] Lena: how granular is token accounting? some providers roll everything up.
[04:01] Maya: token accounting is per-request with normalization across model tokenizers — we show normalized token count and cost attribution. caveat: tokenizer mismatches can introduce small diffs, we flag those.
[04:12] Samir: about Optimize — what kind of recs will we see for batching vs latency?
[04:16] Evan: Optimize runs a lightweight workload analysis on sample traces: it recommends batch size targets, whether prefix or KV caching will help, and suggests quantization levels for each route given your SLOs. recommendations include expected cost delta and estimated risk to p95.
[04:29] Rajiv: do you have real examples?
[04:31] Maya: here's a prior customer where batching plus KV caching cut per-token compute by 40% with minimal impact to p95 because it was mostly stateless short requests. we'll include a case study link.
[04:42] Samir: ok interesting. what about billing export? we need a csv with route-level cost attribution for our finance system.
[04:49] Maya: Billing -> Exports. you can configure daily exports with route, org_id, model_variant, tokens, cost columns. sample export link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/exports (doc link, sandbox only).
[05:00] Aisha: our billing owner will need invoices mapped to our GL codes; can Redwood support custom fields?
[05:05] Jordan: yes custom billing fields and chargeback mapping are supported via the exports and an API. we'll include an example mapping in the pilot packet.
[05:13] -- Security deep dive (short) --
[05:15] Rajiv: can you walk through logs and retention — we want redacted request logs and 90 day retention for full traces and longer for aggregated metrics.
[05:23] Maya: you can configure retention per environment: short retention for raw transcripts, longer for aggregated metrics. redaction rules can be applied at the gateway so no raw PII leaves the stack.
[05:33] Lena: about on-prem: does the control plane still need connectivity to Redwood for updates?
[05:37] Jordan: Private mode has a customer-controlled control plane; it can be air-gapped with manual updates, or virtual private link. details depend on the package.
[05:46] -- Objection/Procurement questions --
[05:48] Aisha: pilot procurement — what's the billing model for pilots? short term credits or PO?
[05:53] Jordan: typically we do a hosted pilot on usage billing with a credit cap, or reserved mini-dedicated for heavier load. we'll propose both in pricing doc.
[05:59] Samir: timeline — we want to run a 4-week pilot and evaluate cost savings and latency compliance. can you commit to a 4 week window starting mid-April?
[06:07] Jordan: yes that sounds doable. we'll aim for pilot kickoff week of April 13.
[06:12] -- Recap and next steps --
[06:15] Jordan: quick recap: we'll send pilot pricing + model matrix; Maya will provision sandbox and dashboard templates; Chorus to give workloads and success metrics; we'll schedule kickoff.
[06:25] Samir: perfect, please include security doc and SOC2 cert in the packet.
[06:29] Jordan: will do. any final Qs?
[06:32] Rajiv: minor: can we programmatically adjust routing policies via api? we want infra to update tiers automatically.
[06:38] Maya: yes, policies are available via the Redwood API and via console; we'll share a short swagger snippet.
[06:44] Aisha: thanks everyone.
[06:46] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread.
